- When sentiment is high (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peaks by 20–40% if preceded by strong sentiment.
- If model shows sharp upward spikes (e.g., >3x recent mean), it often overshoots; cap such forecasts at 1.5x recent 7-day average unless sentiment is strongly bullish.
- When sentiment is low (≤0.33) and prices are falling, model underestimates downside; add 10–30% buffer to negative deviations for low-sentiment periods.
- Model often underreacts to sentiment shifts; if sentiment turns bullish within 3 days, adjust forecast to reflect 1–2 day lag in price response.
- For 30-day horizon, model frequently overestimates early periods (days 1–7) when sentiment is volatile; apply 15–25% downward correction to first 7 days if sentiment is mixed or negative.
- If sentiment history shows repeated 0.00 values, model tends to underforecast; apply 10–20% upward bias to all forecasts if sentiment is consistently neutral or negative.
